problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a series of shipment parcels into standardized delivery trucks. The parcels are as follows:

* Parcel Alpha: volume 50 cubic feet
* Parcel Beta: volume 40 cubic feet
* Parcel Gamma: volume 31 cubic feet
* Parcel Delta: volume 50 cubic feet
* Parcel Epsilon: volume 61 cubic feet
* Parcel Zeta: volume 34 cubic feet
* Parcel Eta: volume 65 cubic feet
* Parcel Theta: volume 69 cubic feet
* Parcel Iota: volume 55 cubic feet
* Parcel Kappa: volume 49 cubic feet
* Parcel Lambda: volume 66 cubic feet
* Parcel Mu: volume 64 cubic feet
* Parcel Nu: volume 41 cubic feet
* Parcel Xi: volume 44 cubic feet
* Parcel Omicron: volume 31 cubic feet
* Parcel Pi: volume 60 cubic feet
* Parcel Rho: volume 37 cubic feet
* Parcel Sigma: volume 43 cubic feet
* Parcel Tau: volume 58 cubic feet
* Parcel Upsilon: volume 48 cubic feet
* Parcel Phi: volume 67 cubic feet
* Parcel Chi: volume 49 cubic feet
* Parcel Psi: volume 48 cubic feet
* Parcel Omega: volume 30 cubic feet
* Parcel A1: volume 69 cubic feet
* Parcel B1: volume 52 cubic feet
* Parcel C1: volume 47 cubic feet
* Parcel D1: volume 35 cubic feet
* Parcel E1: volume 30 cubic feet
* Parcel F1: volume 68 cubic feet
* Parcel G1: volume 31 cubic feet
* Parcel H1: volume 59 cubic feet
* Parcel I1: volume 33 cubic feet
* Parcel J1: volume 39 cubic feet
* Parcel K1: volume 35 cubic feet
* Parcel L1: volume 33 cubic feet
* Parcel M1: volume 46 cubic feet
* Parcel N1: volume 49 cubic feet

Each delivery truck possesses a maximum volumetric capacity of 100 cubic feet. The objective is to assign every parcel to a truck such that the total volumetric load in any given truck does not surpass its limit, with each parcel being allocated to precisely one truck. The overarching aim is to accomplish this distribution utilizing the minimal possible number of trucks.
